````
---
# Claude Code Setup Plugin

Analyze codebases and recommend tailored Claude Code automations - hooks, skills, MCP servers, and more.

## What It Does

Claude uses this skill to scan your codebase and recommend the top 1-2 automations in each category:

- **MCP Servers** - External integrations (context7 for docs, Playwright for frontend)
- **Skills** - Packaged expertise (Plan agent, frontend-design)
- **Hooks** - Automatic actions (auto-format, auto-lint, block sensitive files)
- **Subagents** - Specialized reviewers (security, performance, accessibility)
- **Slash Commands** - Quick workflows (/test, /pr-review, /explain)

This skill is **read-only** - it analyzes but doesn't modify files.

## Usage

```
"recommend automations for this project"
"help me set up Claude Code"
"what hooks should I use?"
```
````

````markdown
---
name: claude-automation-recommender
description: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash
---

# Claude Automation Recommender

Analyze codebase patterns to recommend tailored Claude Code automations across all extensibility options.

**This skill is read-only.** It analyzes the codebase and outputs recommendations. It does NOT create or modify any files. Users implement the recommendations themselves or ask Claude separately to help build them.

## Output Guidelines

- **Recommend 1-2 of each type**: Don't overwhelm - surface the top 1-2 most valuable automations per category
- **If user asks for a specific type**: Focus only on that type and provide more options (3-5 recommendations)
- **Go beyond the reference lists**: The reference files contain common patterns, but use web search to find recommendations specific to the codebase's tools, frameworks, and libraries
- **Tell users they can ask for more**: End by noting they can request more recommendations for any specific category

## Automation Types Overview

| Type | Best For |
|------|----------|
| **Hooks** | Automatic actions on tool events (format on save, lint, block edits) |
| **Subagents** | Specialized reviewers/analyzers that run in parallel |
| **Skills** | Packaged expertise, workflows, and repeatable tasks (invoked by Claude or user via `/skill-name`) |
| **Plugins** | Collections of skills that can be installed |
| **MCP Servers** | External tool integrations (databases, APIs, browsers, docs) |

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Codebase Analysis

Gather project context:

```bash
# Detect project type and tools
ls -la package.json pyproject.toml Cargo.toml go.mod pom.xml 2>/dev/null
cat package.json 2>/dev/null | head -50

# Check dependencies for MCP server recommendations
cat package.json 2>/dev/null | grep -E '"(react|vue|angular|next|express|fastapi|django|prisma|supabase|stripe)"'

# Check for existing Claude Code config
ls -la .claude/ CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null

# Analyze project structure
ls -la src/ app/ lib/ tests/ components/ pages/ api/ 2>/dev/null
```

**Key Indicators to Capture:**

| Category | What to Look For | Informs Recommendations For |
|----------|------------------|----------------------------|
| Language/Framework | package.json, pyproject.toml, import patterns | Hooks, MCP servers |
| Frontend stack | React, Vue, Angular, Next.js | Playwright MCP, frontend skills |
| Backend stack | Express, FastAPI, Django | API documentation tools |
| Database | Prisma, Supabase, raw SQL | Database MCP servers |
| External APIs | Stripe, OpenAI, AWS SDKs | context7 MCP for docs |
| Testing | Jest, pytest, Playwright configs | Testing hooks, subagents |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions, CircleCI | GitHub MCP server |
| Issue tracking | Linear, Jira references | Issue tracker MCP |
| Docs patterns | OpenAPI, JSDoc, docstrings | Documentation skills |

### Phase 2: Generate Recommendations

Based on analysis, generate recommendations across all categories:

#### A. MCP Server Recommendations

See [references/mcp-servers.md](references/mcp-servers.md) for detailed patterns.

| Codebase Signal | Recommended MCP Server |
|-----------------|------------------------|
| Uses popular libraries (React, Express, etc.) | **context7** - Live documentation lookup |
| Frontend with UI testing needs | **Playwright** - Browser automation/testing |
| Uses Supabase | **Supabase MCP** - Direct database operations |
| PostgreSQL/MySQL database | **Database MCP** - Query and schema tools |
| GitHub repository | **GitHub MCP** - Issues, PRs, actions |
| Uses Linear for issues | **Linear MCP** - Issue management |
| AWS infrastructure | **AWS MCP** - Cloud resource management |
| Slack workspace | **Slack MCP** - Team notifications |
| Memory/context persistence | **Memory MCP** - Cross-session memory |
| Sentry error tracking | **Sentry MCP** - Error investigation |
| Docker containers | **Docker MCP** - Container management |

#### B. Skills Recommendations

See [references/skills-reference.md](references/skills-reference.md) for details.

Create skills in `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Some are also available via plugins:

| Codebase Signal | Skill | Plugin |
|-----------------|-------|--------|
| Building plugins | skill-development | plugin-dev |
| Git commits | commit | commit-commands |
| React/Vue/Angular | frontend-design | frontend-design |
| Automation rules | writing-rules | hookify |
| Feature planning | feature-dev | feature-dev |

**Custom skills to create** (with templates, scripts, examples):

| Codebase Signal | Skill to Create | Invocation |
|-----------------|-----------------|------------|
| API routes | **api-doc** (with OpenAPI template) | Both |
| Database project | **create-migration** (with validation script) | User-only |
| Test suite | **gen-test** (with example tests) | User-only |
| Component library | **new-component** (with templates) | User-only |
| PR workflow | **pr-check** (with checklist) | User-only |
| Releases | **release-notes** (with git context) | User-only |
| Code style | **project-conventions** | Claude-only |
| Onboarding | **setup-dev** (with prereq script) | User-only |

#### C. Hooks Recommendations

See [references/hooks-patterns.md](references/hooks-patterns.md) for configurations.

| Codebase Signal | Recommended Hook |
|-----------------|------------------|
| Prettier configured | PostToolUse: auto-format on edit |
| ESLint/Ruff configured | PostToolUse: auto-lint on edit |
| TypeScript project | PostToolUse: type-check on edit |
| Tests directory exists | PostToolUse: run related tests |
| `.env` files present | PreToolUse: block `.env` edits |
| Lock files present | PreToolUse: block lock file edits |
| Security-sensitive code | PreToolUse: require confirmation |

#### D. Subagent Recommendations

See [references/subagent-templates.md](references/subagent-templates.md) for templates.

| Codebase Signal | Recommended Subagent |
|-----------------|---------------------|
| Large codebase (>500 files) | **code-reviewer** - Parallel code review |
| Auth/payments code | **security-reviewer** - Security audits |
| API project | **api-documenter** - OpenAPI generation |
| Performance critical | **performance-analyzer** - Bottleneck detection |
| Frontend heavy | **ui-reviewer** - Accessibility review |
| Needs more tests | **test-writer** - Test generation |

#### E. Plugin Recommendations

See [references/plugins-reference.md](references/plugins-reference.md) for available plugins.

| Codebase Signal | Recommended Plugin |
|-----------------|-------------------|
| General productivity | **anthropic-agent-skills** - Core skills bundle |
| Document workflows | Install docx, xlsx, pdf skills |
| Frontend development | **frontend-design** plugin |
| Building AI tools | **mcp-builder** for MCP development |

### Phase 3: Output Recommendations Report

Format recommendations clearly. **Only include 1-2 recommendations per category** - the most valuable ones for this specific codebase. Skip categories that aren't relevant.

```markdown

## Decision Framework

### When to Recommend MCP Servers
- External service integration needed (databases, APIs)
- Documentation lookup for libraries/SDKs
- Browser automation or testing
- Team tool integration (GitHub, Linear, Slack)
- Cloud infrastructure management

### When to Recommend Skills

- Document generation (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf — also in plugins)
- Frequently repeated prompts or workflows
- Project-specific tasks with arguments
- Applying templates or scripts to tasks (skills can bundle supporting files)
- Quick actions invoked with `/skill-name`
- Workflows that should run in isolation (`context: fork`)

**Invocation control:**
- `disable-model-invocation: true` — User-only (for side effects: deploy, commit, send)
- `user-invocable: false` — Claude-only (for background knowledge)
- Default (omit both) — Both can invoke

### When to Recommend Hooks
- Repetitive post-edit actions (formatting, linting)
- Protection rules (block sensitive file edits)
- Validation checks (tests, type checks)

### When to Recommend Subagents
- Specialized expertise needed (security, performance)
- Parallel review workflows
- Background quality checks

### When to Recommend Plugins
- Need multiple related skills
- Want pre-packaged automation bundles
- Team-wide standardization

---

## Configuration Tips

### MCP Server Setup

**Team sharing**: Check `.mcp.json` into repo so entire team gets same MCP servers

**Debugging**: Use `--mcp-debug` flag to identify configuration issues

**Prerequisites to recommend:**
- GitHub CLI (`gh`) - enables native GitHub operations
- Puppeteer/Playwright CLI - for browser MCP servers

### Headless Mode (for CI/Automation)

Recommend headless Claude for automated pipelines:

```bash
# Pre-commit hook example
claude -p "fix lint errors in src/" --allowedTools Edit,Write

# CI pipeline with structured output
claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format stream-json | your_command
```

### Permissions for Hooks

Configure allowed tools in `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Edit", "Write", "Bash(npm test:*)", "Bash(git commit:*)"]
  }
}
```
````

```
## M10 at a glance

M10 is the **second end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform, and
the first to exercise the **notebook-submission / kernel-push** path.
M9 validated the CSV-submission path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`) on Spaceship Titanic. M10 validates the
notebook-submission path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` →
kernel run → public LB) on Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU
(`tpu-getting-started`).

Petals to the Metal is "Getting Started" tier: multi-class image
classification over 104 flower species, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a single real kernel push under
explicit human approval. TPU is optional — Kaggle accepts GPU-backed
notebooks for this competition too — so the baseline can run locally
and only the kernel runner needs Kaggle's hardware.

M10 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the kernel-push loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval
gates*, not that the LB score is high. The CV / holdout thresholds in
```

```
# AGENTS.md — Cross-Tool Project Instructions

This repository builds a hybrid human + AI coding agent for Kaggle-style competitions and authorized CTF/lab challenges.

## Two meanings of "code agent"

**Platform-development coding agents** are external AI tools — Claude Code (primary), ChatGPT, Cursor — used to build this repository. They write source code, update docs, run local tests, and open PRs under human supervision.

**Runtime competition code agents** are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete. Initial runtime: Claude Agent SDK in an isolated Python worker. Future: model router for Claude, GPT-style, and local models.

Never confuse the two. A platform-development agent editing this repo is not the same as a runtime agent running a Kaggle experiment. See `docs/architecture/platform-vs-runtime-agents.md` for details.

## Source of truth
Use this repository as the durable project memory. Do not rely on hidden memory in any single AI product. Important decisions must be written to:
- `PROJECT_STATE.md`
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/architecture/`
- `docs/tooling/`
- `docs/testing/`
- `docs/meeting-notes/`

## Architecture
- Claude Code CLI/Desktop is used for interactive repository development.
- Claude Agent SDK is the intended core production worker.
- Worker execution is Python-first for Kaggle/ML/CTF tasks.
- Control plane and future UI are TypeScript/Supabase, developed in Claude Code (same repo, same migrations, same CI).
- Supabase stores metadata, messages, research notes, runs, results, artifacts, approvals, and audit events.
- Git stores code and agent instructions.
- Large datasets and generated artifacts should not be committed unless explicitly required.

## Branch and worktree rules
- Every AI task that modifies code should use a dedicated branch or worktree.
- `main` must remain stable and protected.
- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch or files simultaneously.
- Do not push branches or create PRs without explicit human approval.
- Do not force-push, reset --hard, or run destructive git operations without explicit human approval.

## Development rules
- Make small, reviewable changes. One meaningful change per task.
- Return a plan and wait for human approval before editing files.
- Update docs and ADRs when changing architecture or workflow assumptions.
- Prefer deterministic tests and local validation before external submissions.
- Never read, print, or commit secrets, `.env`, `kaggle.json`, API keys, or private keys.
- Do not submit to Kaggle or push remote kernels without explicit human approval.
- CTF support is restricted to explicitly authorized challenges, local labs, or sandboxed environments.

## Competition loop
Follow this loop unless a task says otherwise:
1. Understand rules, metric, data, limits, and submission format.
2. Create or verify validation strategy.
3. Establish a baseline.
4. Run one controlled experiment at a time.
5. Record config, metrics, artifacts, logs, and conclusions.
6. Decide whether to iterate, stop, or request human approval for submission.

## Tooling
Existing Kaggle scripts should be wrapped behind stable commands or typed tools. Every tool must document:
- Purpose.
- Inputs and outputs.
- Side effects.
- Safety class: read-only, local-write, remote-write, or submission.
- Required approval policy.

## GitHub collaboration interface
GitHub Issues, labels, PR reviews, and comments are the shared interface
between humans and AI agents working on this repo. The full model lives
in `docs/engineering-practice.md`; the routing rules below are binding.

- **AI implementation is gated by labels.** An agent may pick up an issue
  only when all are true: open, has `ai:ready`, has clear acceptance
  criteria, has an owner/reviewer, and (if `type:decision` ever applied)
  the decision is `decision:confirmed`. If any of these is missing, the
  issue stays `ai:blocked` or `decision:needed`.
- **Triage is read-write on labels and comments only**, and only when the
  rule is deterministic. Triage agents must not infer decisions from
  ambiguous comments — file `decision:needed` instead.
- **Remote writes require explicit human approval.** This covers
  `gh issue edit/comment/close`, `gh pr edit/comment/merge/create`,
  `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh release *`, `git push`, and any
  mass label/issue mutation. `scripts/sync_labels.py` defaults to
```

> | **security-reviewer** subagent role | `safety-guard` agent + `guard_tool.py` Pre-hook |
> | **test-writer / code-reviewer** subagent | `test-coverage-reviewer`, plus `Agent(Plan)` / `Agent(Explore)` allowlisted |
> | **PreToolUse block `.env` / lock files** | `permissions.deny` covers `.env*`, `kaggle.json`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, force-push, `sudo`, IMDS hosts |
> | **PreToolUse: block kaggle submit / kernel push without approval** | `guard_tool.py` regex blocks `kaggle kernels push`, `kca kaggle submit/push/upload`, `supabase db push/reset` |
> | **PostToolUse: audit/telemetry** | `audit_event.py` on Bash|Edit|Write + ConfigChange |
> | **inventory-drift / labels-sync skills** | already in `.claude/skills/` |
> | **Headless mode for CI** | already invoked from `.github/workflows/claude*.yml` |
> | **Supabase migration discipline** | covered by `docs/milestones.md` + manual review (not a discrete skill, but flow exists) |
> 
> ### New, safe, additive recommendations
> | # | Type | Recommendation | Why it adds value here |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | **R1** | MCP server | **context7** | Live docs for `psycopg`, `nbformat`, Kaggle API, Anthropic SDK during ML/agent work. Pure read; no write side effects. |
> | **R2** | MCP server | **Supabase MCP** (read-only mode) | Schema introspection for `supabase/migrations/000{1..7}*.sql` from agent context, *only if scoped to local container DSN* — `KCA_DB_TARGET=local`. Must NOT use cloud project token. |
> | **R3** | Hook | **PostToolUse: `ruff check --fix` then `ruff format` on `*.py` Edit/Write** | `ruff` already a dev dep; CI may flag style late. Lints+formats at edit time — local-only, idempotent. |
> | **R4** | Hook | **PostToolUse: `pytest -q tests/<related>` on touched tests** | Tests exist (`pyproject.toml: testpaths = ["tests"]`). Gives faster signal than full `pytest` in goal mode. Scope by changed paths only to keep it cheap. |
> | **R5** | Hook (Pre) | **Block `git push origin main` / `git push.*\bmain\b`** | Reinforces `AGENTS.md` "do not push to main" rule. `guard_tool.py` already blocks `--force` but not branch-target. |
> | **R6** | Skill | **create-supabase-migration** | Templates the `supabase/migrations/NNNN_<topic>.sql` numbering, `BEGIN; … COMMIT;` shape, and the local-vs-remote application split per memory `reference_supabase_db`. |
> | **R7** | Skill | **kca-cli-helper** (Claude-only) | Background skill that captures the `python tools/kca/kca.py …` subcommand surface so agents don't re-read `tools/kca/COMMANDS.md` each turn. Already partially in `kaggle-tooling-integration`; could be split or merged. |
> | **R8** | Slash command | **/m9.6-coverage** or generic **/coverage-gap** | Hook into existing `test-coverage-reviewer` agent without manual subagent spawn. Pure invocation sugar. |
> 
> ### Unsafe or not applicable
> | Skill recommendation | Why we're skipping |
> |---|---|
> | **Playwright MCP** / `frontend-design` plugin / `ui-reviewer` subagent | No frontend in the repo; control-plane UI is future work. |
> | **GitHub MCP server** | Duplicates the already-allowlisted `gh` CLI — adds a token surface (write scopes) on top of the existing approval gates. `feedback_permissive_github_dev_phase` already loosens `gh` writes deterministically. |
> | **Auto-format/auto-lint on Markdown / SQL** | Migrations are append-only and reviewed by humans; auto-rewriting SQL hooks risks corrupting history-sensitive files. |
> | **Memory MCP server** | We already have auto-memory + Supabase metadata — adding another memory store fragments the source of truth (`AGENTS.md`: "Use this repository as the durable project memory"). |
> | **Slack / Linear / Sentry MCPs** | No project use today; would add external network egress beyond the sandbox allowlist. |
> | **AWS / Docker MCP** | Out of scope; `docker compose` is already allowlisted for the Supabase container only. |
> | **`claude -p` headless inside hooks for "fix lint errors"** | Recursive Claude invocations from hooks are explicitly the kind of thing `guard_tool.py` does not anticipate; surprise spend, no audit. |
> | **PreToolUse "require confirmation on security-sensitive code"** | Overlaps with `permissions.ask` list; adding another layer would just produce double-prompts. |
